mainTopic: Stories and rules of כיבוד אב ואם: personal service, honor in life and death, and the definitions of מורא and כיבוד
overview: This amud is full of stories and teachings about כיבוד אב ואם. רבי אבהו praises his son אבימי, who personally ran to open the door for him and stood over him while he slept. אביי tells רב יעקב בר אבוה he may accept service from his mother but not from his father, a תלמיד חכם. רבי טרפון is told that letting his mother step on him is not even half of כיבוד, and רב יוסף would stand up for his mother as if for the שכינה. רב אסי leaves his elderly mother for ארץ ישראל. When she follows him, he asks רבי יוחנן whether he may go out to meet her, and רבי יוחנן answers only with a blessing, which רבי אלעזר reads as permission. Then a ברייתא teaches how to honor a father in life and after death. Another ברייתא explains that a חכם does not say his father's name plainly, though his תורגמן may. The amud ends by defining מורא and כיבוד and opening a new question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Grinding with a millstone can bring a son to the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a teaching from just before this point: a son who has his father grind at a millstone can still earn עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and he brings him to the life of the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that started just before this line. It says that a son who gives his father hard work, in the right spirit, can earn עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full teaching contrasts two sons. One feeds his father fine food but in a bad way and is punished. The other has his father grind at a mill, but does it with care and respect, and is rewarded. What counts is the attitude behind what the son does, not how fancy it looks.

keyTerms.meaning: The life of the World to Come

phrases.english: and brings him to the life of the World to Come.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before: the son who makes his father grind at a millstone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the teaching contrasting two ways of treating a father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: How a son treats his father, even with hard labor, can earn him עולם הבא if it is done with respect.

steps.title: רבי אבהו points to his son as a model of honoring parents
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says that his son אבימי is a true example of someone who fulfilled the מצוה of כיבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: someone like my son אבימי fulfilled the מצוה of honoring parents.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו names his own son אבימי as an example of doing כיבוד אב properly. This sets up the stories that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after a teaching about attitude in serving a parent, the גמרא gives a real-life model. The stories that come next show what אבימי did that earned this praise.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
such as Avimi, my son,
fulfilled the מצוה of honoring.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ כְּגוֹן אֲבִימִי בְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a living example of proper כיבוד אב after the general teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבימי is held up as a model of כיבוד אב ואם.

steps.title: אבימי runs to open the door for his father
steps.stepSummary: Though אבימי had five ordained sons, he himself ran to open the door for רבי אבהו and called out 'Yes, yes' on the way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי had five ordained sons while his father was alive. Still, when רבי אבהו came and called at the gate, אבימי himself ran to open it, saying 'Yes, yes!' until he got there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the first story showing how אבימי honored his father. He didn't send one of his important sons. He ran to the door himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail about five ordained sons shows that אבימי had plenty of distinguished people who could have opened the door. Yet he did it personally. He also called out right away so his father would not feel ignored while waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordained (given סמיכה to rule on halacha)

phrases.english: Five ordained sons he had,
Avimi did, during his father's lifetime,
and when Rabbi Abbahu would come
and call at the gate,
he would run and go and open for him,
and say: Yes, yes,
until he reached there.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַמְשָׁה בְּנֵי סְמִיכִי הֲוָה לֵיהּ לַאֲבִימִי בְּחַיֵּי אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבי אבהו's praise of אבימי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proper כיבוד means doing it personally and with eagerness, even for a great person.

steps.title: אבימי waits over his sleeping father and is rewarded
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asked for water and fell asleep before it came. אבימי stood bent over him until he woke, and was rewarded with success in explaining מזמור לאסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day רבי אבהו said to him: 'Give me water to drink.' By the time אבימי brought it, his father had dozed off. אבימי stood bent over him until he woke up. Heaven helped him, and אבימי was able to explain the psalm 'מזמור לאסף'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about אבימי's כיבוד אב. Then it tells his reward: help from heaven in his Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימי didn't put the water down and leave. He stayed standing, ready to serve the moment his father woke. The גמרא links this to a reward: his learning succeeded, and he could explain a hard פרק of תהלים.
steps.whatToRemember: אבימי, a great scholar, personally served his father: running to the door and standing over him while he slept. His reward was success in Torah learning.

phrases.english: One day he said to him:
Give me water to drink.
By the time he brought it to him, he had dozed off.
He bent over and stood over him
until he woke up.
His matter was helped,
and Avimi expounded "A psalm of Asaph."

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַשְׁקְיַין מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about אבימי, adding the reward he received.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Patient, devoted כיבוד אב is rewarded with heavenly help in Torah.

steps.title: May a son let his parents serve him?
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב בר אבוה asks אביי what to do when his father hands him a cup and his mother pours for him on his return from the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב בר אבוה said to אביי: 'Take someone like me. When I come home from the study hall, my father hands me a cup and my mother pours for me. What should I do?'
steps.whatsHappening: A practical question comes up: a son whose parents lovingly serve him asks whether he is allowed to accept it. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stories so far show a son serving his parents. Here it's the other way around: the parents want to serve the son. The question is whether accepting their kindness goes against כיבוד אב ואם.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אֲבוּהּ לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Ya'akov bar Avuh said to Abaye:
For someone such as me,
for whom, by the time I come from the study hall,
my father hands me a cup
and my mother pours for me,
how should I act?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אֲבוּהּ לְאַבָּיֵי כְּגוֹן אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stories of a son serving to the reverse case of parents serving the son.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a son may accept service from his father and mother.

steps.title: Accept from your mother, not from your father
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that he may accept from his mother but not from his father, because his father is a תלמיד חכם and would be hurt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: 'Accept it from your mother, but don't accept it from your father. Since he is a Torah scholar, he will feel hurt.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a split answer: accepting from the mother is fine, but accepting from the father is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is the father's feelings as a בר תורה. He would be pained by being treated in a way that doesn't fit the respect owed to him. So whether you may accept a parent's kindness depends on whether accepting it would hurt that parent.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind is weakened: he feels hurt

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: a son may accept service from his mother, but not from his father who is a תלמיד חכם, since the father would feel hurt.

phrases.english: He said to him: From your mother, accept,
but from your father do not accept,
for since he is a Torah scholar,
he will be disheartened.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מֵאִמָּךְ קַבֵּיל וּמֵאֲבוּךְ לָא תְּקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יעקב בר אבוה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Accept from the mother. Do not accept from the father, a Torah scholar, because he would be hurt.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that כיבוד takes into account the parent's feelings and standing, not only the son's actions.

steps.title: רבי טרפון lets his mother step on him
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון bent down so his mother could climb onto and down from her bed by stepping on him, and he praised himself for it in the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון had a mother. Whenever she wanted to get into bed, he bent down so she could climb up on him. Whenever she wanted to get down, she stepped down onto him. He came to the בית מדרש and praised himself for this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about how far רבי טרפון went in honoring his mother. It ends with him praising himself, which sets up the reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון used his own body as a step stool for his mother, which looks like the highest level of כיבוד. His praising himself is the key detail, because the next step will tell him he has not reached even half.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהִיא אִמָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon had a certain mother
that whenever she wished
to go up into bed
he would bend down and help her go up,
and whenever she would come down,
she would step down onto him.
He came and praised himself in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהִיא אִמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another story to the series of stories about כיבוד אב ואם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון served as a step for his mother and was proud of it.

steps.title: Not even half of the honor
steps.stepSummary: The scholars tell רבי טרפון that he has not reached half of כיבוד. The real test is whether he would stay silent if she threw his wallet into the sea in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You have not yet reached even half of honoring her. Has she ever thrown your wallet into the sea in front of you, and you did not embarrass her?
steps.whatsHappening: The people in the בית מדרש push back on רבי טרפון's self-praise. They say physical service is not the hardest part of כיבוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Helping a parent with your body is hard, but the scholars point to something harder: losing money because of a parent and still not shaming them. Their example is a mother who throws her son's purse into the sea in front of him.
steps.confusionAlert: They are not saying רבי טרפון did anything wrong. They are saying the מצוה demands even more than what he did, so there is no room to feel proud.

phrases.english: They said to him:
You still have not reached half of the honor.
Has she ever thrown a wallet into the sea in front of you
and you did not embarrass her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי טרפון's claim that he had fully done the מצוה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי טרפון's self-praise that he had reached the full measure of כיבוד.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Bodily service is not the peak. Not shaming a parent who causes you real loss is greater.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that the core of כיבוד is controlling your reaction and protecting the parent's dignity, not only physical help.

steps.title: רב יוסף stands for the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: When רב יוסף heard his mother's footsteps, he would say he was standing up before the arriving שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יוסף heard the sound of his mother's footsteps, he would say: Let me stand up before the שכינה that is coming.
steps.whatsHappening: Another short story. רב יוסף, who was blind, treated his mother's arrival as if the שכינה itself were coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the mindset behind כיבוד. Because ה׳ is a partner with the parents in creating a person, honoring a parent is like honoring the שכינה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef, when he would hear
the sound of his mother's footsteps, would say:
I will stand before the Divine Presence that is coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף כִּי הֲוָה שָׁמַע קָל כַּרְעָא דְאִמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of stories about honoring parents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A parent's presence is to be treated like the presence of the שכינה.

steps.title: Fortunate is one who never saw his parents
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that a person who never saw his parents is fortunate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Fortunate is the one who never saw them, meaning his parents.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reacts to how demanding כיבוד is. He says it is a blessing never to have known one's parents, since then one cannot fail in honoring them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the stories showing how high the bar is, רבי יוחנן admits that fully meeting it is almost impossible. Someone without living parents is spared the risk of falling short.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Fortunate is one who did not see them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means his father and mother. Honoring them properly is so hard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the stories that showed how hard כיבוד is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since כיבוד אב ואם is so hard to fulfill fully, one who never saw his parents is fortunate.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and אביי never knew their parents
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's father died while his mother was pregnant, and his mother died giving birth. The same was true of אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן's mother was pregnant with him, his father died. When she gave birth to him, his mother died. The same happened with אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives background showing that רבי יוחנן was speaking from his own life. He never saw either parent, and neither did אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why רבי יוחנן said 'fortunate is one who never saw them.' It also adds a claim about אביי, which the גמרא will question in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּי עִבְּרַתּוּ אִמּוֹ – מֵת אָבִיו,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan: when his mother became pregnant with him, his father died,
when she gave birth to him, his mother died.
And the same was true of Abaye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the personal background behind רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן and אביי both never saw their parents.

steps.title: But אביי often quoted his mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how אביי could have never seen his mother, since he often says 'My mother told me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But אביי often said: My mother told me!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that אביי never knew his mother. It points to his well-known saying, 'My mother told me.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many places in ש״ס, אביי passes on advice he heard from 'my mother.' That seems to contradict the claim that his mother died when he was born.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Abaye say:
My mother told me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim from the previous step that אביי never saw his mother.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement 'וְכֵן אַבָּיֵי', that אביי's mother died at his birth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי often quotes 'my mother', so he must have known a mother.

steps.title: That was his foster mother
steps.stepSummary: The 'mother' אביי quoted was the woman who raised him, not his birth mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: That woman was the one who raised him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. When אביי said 'my mother,' he meant the woman who raised him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'mother' in אביי's sayings refers to his foster mother. So it is still true that his birth mother died when he was born.

keyTerms.meaning: His foster mother, the woman who raised him

steps.whatToRemember: When אביי says 'אֲמַרָה לִי אֵם' anywhere in ש״ס, he is quoting the woman who raised him, not his birth mother.

phrases.english: That was his foster mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about אביי's mother.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: 'mother' means foster mother.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'My mother' means his birth mother, so he must have known her.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'My mother' means the woman who raised him. His birth mother died at his birth.

steps.title: רב אסי and his elderly mother
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי's elderly mother made more and more demands until she wanted a husband as handsome as he was. He left her and went to ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי had an elderly mother. She said to him: I want jewelry. He made it for her. She said: I want a husband. He said: I will look for one for you. She said: I want a husband as handsome as you. He left her and went to ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story. רב אסי tries to meet his elderly mother's requests, but when they become impossible, he leaves for ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first רב אסי does whatever she asks, even promising to find her a husband. Her last request shows that her mind is failing and he cannot satisfy her, so he leaves. This sets up his question to רבי יוחנן.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַסִּי הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהִיא אִמָּא זְקֵינָה.
phrases.english: Rav Asi had an elderly mother.
She said to him: I want jewelry.
He made it for her.
She said: I want a husband.
He said: I will look for one for you.
She said: I want a husband as handsome as you.
phrases.notes: This request showed him her mind was going, and he could never satisfy her.

phrases.english: He left her and went to Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַסִּי הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהִיא אִמָּא זְקֵינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story about a parent whose demands cannot be met.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When his mother's demands became impossible, רב אסי left her and moved to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: May one leave ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: Hearing that his mother was following him, רב אסי asked רבי יוחנן whether one may leave ארץ ישראל for חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: He heard that she was coming after him. He came before רבי יוחנן and asked: What is the law about leaving ארץ ישראל for חוץ לארץ?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי learns that his mother is coming after him. He asks רבי יוחנן a general question first: may a person leave ארץ ישראל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: He starts with the general rule before asking about his own case. This sets up his real question in the next steps.

phrases.english: He heard that she was coming after him.
He came before Rabbi Yoḥanan,
and said to him: What is the law about leaving
from Eretz Yisrael to outside of Eretz Yisrael?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רב אסי story with a question of הלכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether it is allowed to leave ארץ ישראל for חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: It is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that leaving ארץ ישראל for חוץ לארץ is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the general rule: one may not leave ארץ ישראל for חוץ לארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the basic rule without special reasons. It sets the background for רב אסי's follow-up about going to greet his mother.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's general question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leaving ארץ ישראל for חוץ לארץ is forbidden.

steps.title: What about going to greet one's mother?
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי asks whether the rule is different if he is going out to meet his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about going out to greet one's mother?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי now asks about his real case. Is it allowed to leave ארץ ישראל in order to go meet one's mother?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two values collide here: living in ארץ ישראל and כיבוד אם. He wants to know whether כיבוד אם allows leaving.

phrases.english: To go meet a mother, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether כיבוד אם is an exception to the rule just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may leave ארץ ישראל in order to go meet one's mother.

steps.title: I do not know
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he does not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן will not give a clear ruling on this special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is clear, but רבי יוחנן does not say outright whether כיבוד אם overrides it. Steps 19–23 show how his later reply is understood: as a blessing that lets רב אסי go.

phrases.english: He said to him: I do not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's second question without deciding.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No ruling. רבי יוחנן says he does not know.

steps.title: May ה׳ bring you back in peace
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי waited and came back. רבי יוחנן saw that he was set on leaving and blessed him that ה׳ return him in peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: He waited a little and came back. רבי יוחנן said to him: אסי, you have decided to leave. May ה׳ return you in peace.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי comes back again, and רבי יוחנן sees he has made up his mind, so he answers with a blessing instead of a direct ruling. The next steps explain what that blessing meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not say in so many words that it is allowed. He sees that רב אסי is determined and wishes him a safe return. Step 23 explains that this blessing shows he was not angry and was letting him go.

keyTerms.meaning: You have made up your mind

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן first says 'I do not know,' then, seeing רב אסי is determined, sends him off with a blessing. Step 23 shows the blessing meant he approved.

phrases.english: He waited a little, then came back.
He said to him: Asi, you have made up your mind to leave;
may the Omnipresent return you in peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows רבי יוחנן's 'I do not know' with a blessing, whose meaning רבי אלעזר explains in steps 20-23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן does not state a ruling. He sees that רב אסי is determined and blesses him to return in peace. רבי אלעזר will soon explain (step 23) that this blessing means he let him go.

steps.title: רב אסי worries that רבי יוחנן was angry
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי goes to רבי אלעזר and asks whether רבי יוחנן was angry with him for wanting to leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבי אלעזר and said: Heaven forbid, maybe he was angry?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי is unsure what רבי יוחנן's answer meant, so he asks רבי אלעזר whether his teacher was angry with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן never said yes or no about going out to meet a mother. He only gave a blessing. רב אסי is afraid the blessing was a cold way of saying he was upset.

keyTerms.meaning: he was really angry (literally, 'boiling, he boiled')

phrases.english: He (רב אסי) came before רבי אלעזר.
He said to him: Heaven forbid,
perhaps he (רבי יוחנן) was angry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי יוחנן's blessing in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was רבי יוחנן angry that רב אסי wanted to leave ארץ ישראל?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks what exactly was said
steps.stepSummary: Before answering, רבי אלעזר asks for רבי יוחנן's exact words.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What did he say to you?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks a clarifying question. This sets up his answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To judge whether רבי יוחנן was angry, רבי אלעזר needs the actual words. The meaning depends on them.

phrases.english: He (רבי אלעזר) said to him: What did he say to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details before answering step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What were רבי יוחנן's exact words?

steps.title: רב אסי repeats the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי reports that רבי יוחנן said: May the Omnipresent return you in peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'May the Omnipresent return you in peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers רבי אלעזר's question with רבי יוחנן's exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words are a blessing for a safe trip, not a scolding. This sets up רבי אלעזר's conclusion.

phrases.english: He (רב אסי) said to him: May the Omnipresent return you in peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן blessed him that ה׳ return him in peace.

steps.title: A blessing shows there was no anger
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that if רבי יוחנן were angry, he would not have blessed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If he were angry, he would not have blessed you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers רב אסי's worry: the blessing proves רבי יוחנן was not angry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An angry teacher does not send a student off with a blessing. So the blessing means רבי יוחנן was letting him go.

phrases.english: He (רבי אלעזר) said to him: And if it were so that he was angry,
he would not have blessed you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the words from step 22 to answer the worry of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן was not angry; his blessing shows that he allowed the trip.

steps.title: His mother had died: 'Had I known, I would not have left'
steps.stepSummary: Meanwhile רב אסי hears that his mother's coffin is coming, and says that had he known, he would not have left.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the meantime he heard that her coffin was coming. He said: Had I known, I would not have gone out.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רב אסי's mother has died, and he regrets leaving ארץ ישראל, since there was no longer a reason to go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He was leaving only to honor his living mother. Once she died, that reason was gone, so the trip out of ארץ ישראל was no longer needed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's blessing meant permission, but רב אסי's mother died first, so the trip turned out to be unnecessary.

phrases.english: In the meantime
he heard that her coffin was coming.
phrases.notes: 'Her' is his mother. She had died, and her body was being brought to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: He said: Had I known, I would not have gone out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story of רב אסי that began in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reason to leave ארץ ישראל was honoring his living mother. Once she died, he would not have gone.

steps.title: Honor a father both in life and in death
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one must honor his father both while he is alive and after he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: One honors him in his life, and honors him in his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא with a general rule. The next steps explain each half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כיבוד אב does not end when the father dies. The ברייתא names two times of honor and will now give an example of each.

keyTerms.meaning: in his life … in his death

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One honors him (his father) in his life, and honors him in his death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic within כיבוד אב, after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honoring a father applies both during his life and after his death.

steps.title: Honor in life: speak in your father's name
steps.stepSummary: Someone sent on an errand by his father should not push people along 'for my own sake' but 'for Father's sake'.
steps.simpleTranslation: How in his life? One who goes somewhere at his father's word should not say 'Send me off for my sake,' 'Hurry for my sake,' 'Release me for my sake.' Rather, all of them: 'for Father's sake.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the first half: how to honor a father while he is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the son asks people to hurry, he should present the request as his father's. That gives the honor to the father, and people show respect to the father through the son.

phrases.english: How (does one honor him) in his life?
One who goes somewhere at his father's word
should not say: 'Send me off for my own sake,'
'Hurry for my own sake,'
'Release me for my own sake.'
Rather, (he says) all of them: 'for Father's sake.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'in his life' half of step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While his father is alive, a son on his father's errand asks things in his father's name, not his own.

steps.title: Honor in death: add words of respect when quoting him
steps.stepSummary: When quoting his late father, a son says 'So said Father, my teacher, may I be an atonement for his resting place,' not just 'So said Father.'
steps.simpleTranslation: How in his death? If he says something he heard from him, he should not say 'So said Father,' but 'So said Father, my teacher, may I be an atonement for his resting place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the second half: how to honor a father after he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply saying 'Father said' is not enough after death. The son adds a title of respect and offers himself as an atonement for his father's soul.

keyTerms.meaning: may I be an atonement for his resting place

phrases.english: How (does one honor him) in his death?
If he was saying something he heard from his mouth,
he should not say: 'So said Father,'
rather: 'So said Father, my teacher,
may I be an atonement for his resting place.'
phrases.notes: He means: may any suffering due to his father's soul come on me instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'in his death' half of step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After his father's death, a son quotes him with 'Father, my teacher, may I be an atonement for his resting place.'

steps.title: Within twelve months versus after
steps.stepSummary: The 'atonement' wording is only for the first twelve months. After that, he says 'may his memory be for a blessing, for the life of the World to Come.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies within twelve months. From then on, he says: 'May his memory be for a blessing, for the life of the World to Come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The text limits the rule from the last step to the first year after death and gives a different phrase for afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The atonement phrase fits the first twelve months after death. After that, the son switches to a general blessing for his father's memory.

keyTerms.meaning: may his memory be for a blessing

steps.whatToRemember: Honor in life: speak in Father's name. Honor in death: within twelve months say 'may I be an atonement for his resting place'; after that, say 'may his memory be for a blessing.'

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי תּוֹךְ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: And this applies within twelve months (of his death);
from then on, he says:
'May his memory be for a blessing, for the life of the World to Come.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי תּוֹךְ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the wording of step 27 to the first twelve months.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The atonement wording is for twelve months; after that, 'may his memory be for a blessing, for the life of the World to Come.'

steps.title: A חכם changes the name of his father and teacher, a תורגמן does not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a חכם changes his father's and teacher's names when quoting them, but a תורגמן changes neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A חכם changes the name of his father and the name of his teacher. A תורגמן changes neither the name of his father nor the name of his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about quoting a father or teacher by name in a public lecture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of respect, a חכם does not say his father's or teacher's name plainly. The ברייתא says the תורגמן, who passes the lecture on to the crowd, does not change the names. Why the difference is unclear, and the גמרא will now ask about it.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage giving a public lecture
changes the name (does not say it plainly)
the speaker who repeats and explains the sage's words to the crowd

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: חָכָם – מְשַׁנֶּה שֵׁם אָבִיו וְשֵׁם רַבּוֹ.
phrases.english: A חכם changes the name of his father and the name of his teacher.
phrases.notes: He doesn't say his father's or teacher's name plainly when quoting them, as a sign of respect.

phrases.english: A תורגמן does not change

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שֵׁם אָבִיו וְלֹא שֵׁם רַבּוֹ.
phrases.english: neither the name of his father nor the name of his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חָכָם מְשַׁנֶּה שֵׁם אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא, still about honoring a father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם changes his father's and teacher's names when quoting them; a תורגמן does not.

steps.title: Whose father is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which father the ברייתא means when it says the תורגמן does not change the name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question to set up its analysis of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His father' in the תורגמן's half is unclear. It could mean the תורגמן's own father, or the father of the חכם he is repeating.

phrases.english: Whose father (is meant)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of 'his father' in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In the ברייתא, does 'his father' mean the תורגמן's father or the חכם's father?

steps.title: It cannot mean the תורגמן's own father
steps.stepSummary: If it meant the תורגמן's own father, that would be hard: isn't the תורגמן also obligated to honor his father?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the תורגמן's father, is the תורגמן not obligated (in honoring his father)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible reading and pushes it away with a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every son must honor his father, the תורגמן included. So it makes no sense that the תורגמן may say his own father's name plainly when a חכם may not. This reading looks wrong.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a תורגמן is exempt from כיבוד אב. It is saying the opposite: since he is obligated, this reading of the ברייתא cannot be right.

phrases.english: If you say (it means) the father of the תורגמן,

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ תּוּרְגְּמָן לָאו בַּר חִיּוּבָא הוּא?
phrases.english: is the תורגמן not obligated (to honor his father)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא אֲבוּהּ דִּמְתוּרְגְּמָן אַטּוּ תּוּרְגְּמָן לָאו בַּר חִיּוּבָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first answer to the question in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'his father' in the ברייתא as the תורגמן's own father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורגמן must honor his father like everyone else, so he could not be allowed to say his father's name plainly.

steps.title: רבא: it means the Sage's father and teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא is talking about the name of the חכם's father and teacher, not the תורגמן's own father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: the ברייתא means the name of the Sage's father and the name of the Sage's teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the problem from step 31. The 'father' the תורגמן does not rename is the חכם's father, not his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a תורגמן must honor his own father too, so how could he say his father's name plainly? רבא answers that the ברייתא never meant the תורגמן's father. The תורגמן is repeating the חכם's lecture, so the names belong to the חכם's father and teacher. Those people are not the תורגמן's parents, so he may say their names plainly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals that the earlier reading is dropped and a new one is offered.
A Torah scholar who gives the lecture

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
the name of the Sage's father,
phrases.notes: This explains 'the תורגמן does not change' from step 29: it's the lecturing Sage's father, not the תורגמן's own.

phrases.english: and the name of the Sage's teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31 by reading the ברייתא as talking about a different father.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining whose father the ברייתא means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lets the תורגמן say his own father's name plainly, which would clash with his duty to honor his father.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the חכם's father and teacher. The תורגמן owes them no parental honor, so he may say their names plainly.

steps.title: The example of מר בר רב אשי and his speaker
steps.stepSummary: When מר בר רב אשי lectured, he said 'my father, my teacher,' but his speaker said 'So said רב אשי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like מר בר רב אשי. When he lectured at the public lecture, he himself said 'My father, my teacher,' and his speaker said 'So said רב אשי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a real-life example of רבא's explanation. The son used a title, and the speaker used the plain name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר רב אשי was the חכם, and רב אשי was his father. So the son changed the name into a respectful title. The speaker (the תורגמן) was not רב אשי's son, so he said the name plainly. This matches the ברייתא exactly as רבא explained it.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this case. Introduces an example.
The speaker who repeats the lecture aloud to the crowd (the same job as the תורגמן)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Like that of Mar bar Rav Ashi:
when he would lecture at the public lecture,
he would say: "My father, my teacher,"
and his speaker would say:
"So said Rav Ashi."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבא's answer with a real practice.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading: the חכם renames his father, but the תורגמן says the name plainly.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of מר בר רב אשי and his אמורא at the public lecture.

steps.title: What counts as fear and what counts as honor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines מורא of a parent (not standing or sitting in his place, not contradicting him, not deciding his disputes) and כיבוד (feeding, dressing, escorting him).
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: What is fear and what is honor? Fear: he does not stand in his father's place, does not sit in his place, does not contradict his words, and does not decide for him. Honor: he feeds him and gives him drink, dresses and covers him, and brings him in and takes him out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out the two duties a child has toward a parent. It lists what counts as מורא (fear) and what counts as כיבוד (honor).
steps.deeperAnalysis: מורא is a list of things you must NOT do: you may not take the parent's spot or put your judgment over his. כיבוד is a list of things you actively DO: you take care of his needs, like food, clothing, and getting around. The two lists show two separate kinds of מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. Introduces a ברייתא.
Fear or awe of a parent. Mostly things one must hold back from doing.
Honor of a parent. Active care for his needs.
Decides for him. Tips the scales in his argument.

steps.whatToRemember: מורא means don't: don't take his place, contradict him, or judge his arguments. כיבוד means do: feed him, dress him, and escort him.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
What is fear and what is honor?
Fear: he does not stand in his place,
phrases.notes: 'His place' means the father's regular spot.

phrases.english: and does not sit in his place,
and does not contradict his words,
and does not decide for him.
phrases.notes: When his father argues with someone, the son shouldn't step in and announce which side is right.

phrases.english: Honor: he feeds and gives drink,
dresses and covers,
brings in and takes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ מוֹרָא וְאֵיזֶהוּ כִּיבּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: defining the actual duties of fear and honor of parents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מורא: not standing or sitting in the parent's place, not contradicting him, not deciding his disputes. כיבוד: providing food, drink, clothing, and escort.

steps.title: A new question is raised
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that a question was asked of the Sages, setting up the next discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked of them:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to present a new question, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איבעיא להו tells us the Sages had a real doubt they wanted to settle. Right after the ברייתא's list of duties, the question will clear up a detail of those duties.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them. Introduces a real question the Sages were unsure about.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a question that builds on the ברייתא's list of duties.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The question itself comes on the next amud. It is introduced here as a real doubt about the duties just listed.
